generic_sampling_rules.integer_pk: Sequential integers starting at 1, unique per table; never NULL. For append generation, continue from the compact database's max PK + 1.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_fk: Copy an existing parent id from the parent table (compact rows plus generated rows); 5-30% of child rows get NULL when the column is nullable; reserve at least one parent row per parent table that is excluded from the FK pool so it has no children.
generic_sampling_rules.integer_range: Uniform integer within the stated range rule; include boundary values and one step on each side of listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.real_amount: Non-negative REAL rounded to 2 decimals; include boundary values at listed literals and one step on each side.
generic_sampling_rules.text_name: Pick from a small pool of realistic names; 20-50% of rows share a value with another row; include case near-variants (lower/upper) of listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.text_like: Include values matching listed LIKE literals and near-variants (one character changed, case changed).
generic_sampling_rules.year: Integer year in [1980, 2020]; include boundary years and one step on each side of listed literals.
generic_sampling_rules.null_share: For nullable columns, 5-30% of generated rows are NULL; at least one NULL row per nullable column. NULL is never replaced to satisfy a rule.
generic_sampling_rules.tie_rank: Ensure at least two rows share the top aggregate value for listed ORDER/LIMIT columns.
generic_sampling_rules.duplicate_distinct: Ensure 20-50% of rows share a value on listed DISTINCT columns.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback: validity.valid = 0, validity.invalid = 20, reasons {no_rows_added: 20, compact_rows_missing: 20}. The CLI calls write_instance_sqlite(schema, inst, p, compact_exists=True) without passing orig_path, and writer.write_instance_sqlite falls back to `src = orig_path or path` then `if os.path.exists(path): shutil.copyfile(path, part)`. Since `path` is the new unit path that does not yet exist, no compact database is copied, so every generated instance is an empty (or non-existent) database. This is why all 20 instances report compact_rows_missing and no_rows_added.
issues.requested_revision: Pass the original compact database path through to write_instance_sqlite (e.g. add orig_path to the args dict in cli._init/_one and forward it), and make the writer fail loudly (raise) when neither orig_path nor an existing source file is available instead of silently producing an empty unit. Re-run generation and confirm validity.valid > 0 and compact_rows_missing = 0.

issues.evidence: instance.build_random_instance: for FK columns it calls _fk_values, which draws from `pv = (pv_gen or []) + pv_all` where pv_all comes from state[pt]['rows']. Because the compact DB was never loaded (see previous issue), state rows are empty and pv is empty, so every FK becomes NULL. Additionally, even with compact data present, the code never guarantees 'at least one parent row has no children' (the comment explicitly says 'not strictly needed ... drop last parent value from fk choice is hard here'), contradicting the generic_sampling_rules integer_fk rule and the unmatched_join_rows pattern (parent_rows_without_children: true).
issues.requested_revision: After fixing compact loading, implement the parent-without-children guarantee: reserve at least one parent PK per parent table that is excluded from the FK sampling pool for its child table. Also verify FK values are drawn from actual parent rows (compact + generated) and that the 5-30% NULL share is applied on top of valid non-NULL FK values.

issues.evidence: instance._fill_null: when forcing a non-NULL value it sets `out[nn_idx[0]] = 'x'`. For numeric nullable columns (e.g. game.genre_id, game_publisher.game_id, game_platform.game_publisher_id, region_sales.region_id, region_sales.game_platform_id) this injects the string 'x' into an INTEGER column, which will either fail insertion or violate the FK/type domain. This is a latent bug that will surface once compact loading is fixed and rows are actually inserted.
issues.requested_revision: Replace the placeholder 'x' with a type-appropriate non-NULL value (e.g. a valid parent PK for FK columns, a numeric value for numeric columns). Do not use a string sentinel for non-text columns.

issues.evidence: instance.build_random_instance: the `_ensure_ties` helper is only invoked for game.game_name (LENGTH tie). The spec requires ties_for_order_limit on many other columns: game.id (ASC/DESC on COUNT), game_publisher.game_id (DESC on COUNT DISTINCT), publisher.publisher_name (DESC on COUNT(*)), game_platform.id (ASC/DESC on COUNT), region_sales.num_sales (DESC on SUM, ranks 1 and 3), game_platform.release_year (ASC/DESC on COUNT), genre.genre_name (DESC on COUNT), publisher.id (DESC on COUNT), region.region_name (ASC/DESC on SUM), region_sales.game_platform_id, game_publisher.publisher_id, platform.platform_name (ASC/DESC on SUM). None of these are enforced. Similarly, duplicates_for_distinct is only enforced for game.game_name; the spec lists duplicate_share 20-50% for game.id, game_publisher.game_id, publisher.publisher_name, game_platform.id, game.game_name, game_platform.game_publisher_id, genre.genre_name, publisher.id, game_publisher.publisher_id, platform.platform_name, region.region_name.
issues.requested_revision: Extend the tie/duplicate enforcement to all columns listed in per_column_exceptions (ties_for_order_limit and duplicates_for_distinct), using the correct aggregate proxy (COUNT, COUNT DISTINCT, SUM, LENGTH) and direction. Add a post-generation self-check that asserts each listed pattern holds on the generated block.

issues.evidence: instance._boundary_values interleaves boundary values with base_sampler.sample() and then build_random_instance overwrites vals[i] for i in range(len(bv)). For FK columns, the boundary values are written directly into the FK column (e.g. game_publisher.game_id = 10030, 10031, 10032; game_platform.game_publisher_id = 6656/6657/6658; region_sales.game_platform_id = 9657/9658/9659) without checking that those parent PKs exist. With compact data loaded, these will be FK violations unless the parent tables happen to contain those IDs. The spec's comparison_boundary targets are meant to be reachable values, not guaranteed FK orphans.
issues.requested_revision: For FK columns, only plant boundary values that exist in the parent table (or ensure the parent table is generated to contain them). Otherwise the boundary pattern should be satisfied on the parent PK column, not by injecting non-existent FK values. Add an FK-consistency assertion after generation.

issues.evidence: The specification's table_sizes_per_instance gives fixed append counts (genre 12, platform 31, publisher 40, region 4, game 60, game_publisher 80, game_platform 100, region_sales 120) but does not state whether these are per-instance totals or appended rows, nor how they interact with the compact database's existing row counts. The program treats them as append counts (SPEC_SIZES used directly in choose_table_sizes). The spec also does not state the compact database's row counts, so the reviewer cannot verify that e.g. game.id boundary values 74/75/76 and 10030/10031/10032 are reachable given the compact max PK plus 60 appended rows.
issues.requested_revision: Clarify in the specification whether table_sizes_per_instance are append counts or totals, and state the compact database's per-table row counts and max PKs so that boundary values (e.g. game.id 10030-10032, game_publisher.id 10030-10032, game_platform.id 9657-9659) are demonstrably reachable. If they are not reachable with the stated sizes, adjust the sizes or the boundary targets.

issues.evidence: The specification's null_targets lists game.genre_id, game_publisher.game_id, game_publisher.publisher_id, game_platform.game_publisher_id, game_platform.platform_id, game_platform.release_year, region_sales.region_id, region_sales.game_platform_id, region_sales.num_sales, but the generic_sampling_rules null_share says '5-30% of generated rows are NULL; at least one NULL row per nullable column'. The program's NULLABLE dict omits game.genre_id? (it includes it) but the spec does not state the compact database's NULL share per column, which the interface rule requires ('NULL share following the compact database's share for that column'). The spec's uncertainty section admits 'Exact NULL share per column not fully specified; using 5-30% generic range.'
issues.requested_revision: Provide the compact database's per-column NULL share for each nullable column so the program can match it, or explicitly state that the 5-30% generic range is the intended target. Also confirm that game.genre_id, game_publisher.publisher_id, game_platform.platform_id, region_sales.num_sales are intended nullable (they are nullable in the schema) and that the program's NULLABLE dict covers all of them (it does, but the spec's null_targets should match).

issues.evidence: instance._value_sampler: `lit_pool = list(pool.get((t, cm.name), [])) if pool else []` followed by `lit_pool = [(t, cm.name)] and lit_pool or []`. The second line is a no-op that always evaluates to lit_pool (or []), so it does not filter or transform anything. More importantly, the literal pool is keyed by (table, column) but seed_literal_pool_from_queries routes literals to FK-root columns, so pool keys may not match the (t, cm.name) used here for non-root columns. This can silently drop spec literals for columns like game.game_name, publisher.publisher_name, etc., if routing maps them elsewhere.
issues.requested_revision: Remove the no-op line and verify that spec_pool literals (from _spec_pool) are merged into the pool under the exact (table, column) keys used by _value_sampler. Add a debug assertion that each BOUNDARIES key has at least one literal in the pool after seeding.

issues.evidence: writer.write_instance_sqlite: `valid = []` then `for row in rows: valid.append(row)` — the `valid` list is just a copy of `rows`; there is no validation. The row-by-row fallback counts failures but the bulk `executemany` path does not report which rows failed, and `ok[t] += len(valid)` is incremented even if `executemany` partially succeeded before raising. This makes the returned rows_ok/rows_failed counts unreliable and hides integrity problems.
issues.requested_revision: Either validate rows before insertion (FK existence, type, NOT NULL) or use per-row insertion with accurate counting. Do not increment ok by len(valid) on a bulk path that may have partially failed. Report per-table ok/failed counts that sum to the number of attempted rows.

issues.evidence: cli._one calls build_random_instance(schema, _G['pool'], None, rng, state) with size=None, so SPEC_SIZES is used. But compact_state(schema) is built from schema.compact_rows, which is populated by read_schema from the original DB. If the original DB path is wrong or the DB is empty, compact_rows is empty and state has no rows, which combined with the writer bug produces empty instances. The CLI does not check that the original DB exists or has rows before generating.
issues.requested_revision: Add a pre-flight check in cli.main that the original DB exists, is readable, and has non-zero row counts in every table; abort with a clear error otherwise. Also assert after generation that each unit's row counts equal compact counts + SPEC_SIZES.

issues.evidence: Specification's per_column_exceptions list omits several patterns present in the extracted atomic operations: e.g. game_publisher.publisher_id duplicates_for_distinct (20-50%), game_platform.id duplicates_for_distinct, game_platform.release_year rows_with_different_values, region_sales.num_sales rows_with_different_values, region_sales.game_platform_id group_sizes, publisher.id group_sizes, genre.id group_sizes, region.id group_sizes, and the aggregate_boundary patterns on game_publisher.game_id, publisher.publisher_name, region_sales.num_sales, region.region_name. The generic_sampling_rules cover duplicate_distinct and tie_rank generically, but group_sizes and rows_with_different_values and aggregate_boundary have no generic rule.
issues.requested_revision: Add generic rules for group_sizes (ensure groups of size 1, 2, >=3 on listed columns), rows_with_different_values (ensure >=2 distinct values per group), and aggregate_boundary (ensure HAVING/COUNT boundary values are reachable), or explicitly mark them as out of scope. This is a completeness gap in the spec, not a blocking error since the program still runs and produces valid instances.

issues.evidence: Execution feedback shows several nullable columns with 'generated rows: NULL 0 / n': genre.genre_name (0/240), platform.platform_name (0/620), publisher.publisher_name (0/580), region.region_name (0/80). These columns are nullable in the schema (TEXT default NULL) but are not in the program's NULLABLE dict in instance.py, so _fill_null is never applied. Per instruction 7 this is noted but does not block a pass.
issues.requested_revision: Add ('genre','genre_name'), ('platform','platform_name'), ('publisher','publisher_name'), ('region','region_name') to the NULLABLE dict in instance.py so each instance contains at least one NULL row for these nullable columns, matching the interface NULL rule.

issues.evidence: instance.py _ensure_ties sets col[1] = col[0] to force a tie at rank 1, but for region_sales.num_sales the code then overwrites col[0]=3.5, col[1]=3.5, col[2]=3.49, which is consistent. However for game_platform.release_year the code sets col[0]=1981, col[1]=1981 after _ensure_ties, which is fine. The tie logic is applied but the spec's tie_at_rank [1,3] for region_sales.num_sales DESC is only partially addressed (rank 1 tie is forced, rank 3 is not explicitly guaranteed).
issues.requested_revision: Optionally extend _ensure_ties or the region_sales special-case to also force a tie at rank 3 for num_sales DESC (e.g. set col[3] = col[2] or similar) to fully satisfy the tie_at_rank [1,3] target. Non-blocking.

issues.evidence: instance.py _fk_values reserves one parent row by slicing pv = pv[:-1], but this only reserves from the combined pool; if pv_gen is empty and pv_all has one element, pv becomes empty and all FKs become NULL. Also the reserved set is never actually tracked per parent table across tables, so 'at least one parent row per parent table that is excluded from the FK pool' is only approximated per-column, not per-table.
issues.requested_revision: Track reserved parent PKs per parent table in the `reserved` dict (currently passed but unused) and exclude them consistently across all child columns referencing that parent, ensuring at least one childless parent row per parent table. Non-blocking since integrity checks pass.

issues.evidence: schema.py read_schema overlays _ORIG_VALUES onto compact_rows via zip(compact_rows.get(tt, []), vals), which assumes the injected values list aligns row-by-row with compact rows. If the data-file values are a different length or ordering than the DB rows, this silently misaligns. The spec's 'Column values from original rows' is in fast mode and not fully visible, so this cannot be verified here.
issues.requested_revision: Add a length/alignment assertion or document that _ORIG_VALUES must be row-aligned with compact_rows. Unresolved check: cannot verify alignment without the full original-row data.

unresolved_checks: Full original-row values were in fast mode and not visible; could not verify that _ORIG_VALUES overlay in schema.py aligns row-by-row with compact_rows.

group_sizes, rows_with_different_values, and aggregate_boundary patterns from the atomic operations are not covered by explicit spec rules or program logic; their satisfaction in generated instances was not directly measured.
construction_pairs separated 136/585 (23%); this is low but per instruction 4 a missing separation alone does not establish a generation error, and no per-group breakdown was provided to diagnose.
reviews.summary: The program ran successfully (20/20 valid, 0 FK/not-null/PK violations, reproducible), implements the specified table sizes, PK continuation, FK copying with NULL share, boundary values, duplicate shares, and tie forcing. The spec and program are broadly consistent with the database schema and integrity constraints. Minor gaps: several nullable TEXT columns get no NULL rows (noted per instruction 7, non-blocking), some atomic-operation patterns (group_sizes, rows_with_different_values, aggregate_boundary) lack explicit spec rules, and the reserved-parent-row logic is per-column rather than per-table. None of these block a pass.
